subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Tension Structures: When Cables Replace Beams
description: One-minute skill: Tension Structures: When Cables Replace Beams.

hook.text: A steel cable 5 cm thick can support the same load as a steel beam 30 cm deep. Tension is efficient.

buildup.text: Cables carry loads in pure tension — no bending, no buckling. Every atom of steel does useful work.

discovery.text: Tensile structures use membranes stretched between cables. Denver International Airport's roof is Teflon-coated fabric.

twist.text: Tension structures must be pre-stressed or they flap in the wind like sails. Stability requires constant pull.

climax.text: The Munich Olympic Stadium uses a cable-net roof with transparent panels, spanning 75,000 square meters.

punchline.text: Why push when you can pull? Cables do more with less.

quiz.question: Why must tension structures be pre-stressed?
options: Pre-stressing prevents rust from forming on the cables
Without constant pull they would flap in the wind like sails
Pre-stressing reduces the total weight of the cable system
